summary: Blocking sync I/O on the event loop, with a correctly-threadpooled call as the decoy.

must_not_find.why: fetch_logo already dispatches the sync requests call to a threadpool; flagging it means the reviewer pattern-matched on `requests` without reading the wrapper. Every keyword pairs the site with a predicate, so only prose about fetch_logo can produce one — code always writes `fetch_logo(`. Bare `fetch_logo` failed the correct finding instead, whose evidence opens on `logo = await fetch_logo(user.tenant_id)`, the first line of the defective function. `run_in_threadpool` stays — it appears only in the decoy's own body, outside the diff, so only a reviewer that went and quoted the decoy can produce it. Bare `threadpool` is gone: it is the correct finding's own remedy vocabulary.
